messages.text: :wave: piggybacking on the coverage-vs-signal-quality thread from earlier — we ran the Revenue Harness through a full week of low-confidence deal signals and I want to share what actually held up. tl;dr: the *signal decay rate* metric someone mentioned above is the real MVP. code coverage told us almost nothing useful once the inputs got noisy. curious how others are weighting these in their QA rhythm :thread:

this matches what we saw exactly. the thing that finally clicked for us was treating *false positive revival rate* as a first-class metric instead of an afterthought. when the Harness flags a dead deal as "re-engaging" and it's just noise, that erodes rep trust fast — way faster than a missed signal does. we now gate every stress-test pass on it staying under ~8%.

+1 on the trust angle. one rhythm that's working for us: a *Monday calibration pass* where we pull 10 flagged deals and score them as a group before anyone touches their pipeline. it surfaces drift early and keeps everyone honest about what "good signal" actually means. cheap to run, high payoff.

the calibration pass is a great call — we should standardize that. one thing I'd add to the metric set is *time-to-recovery* after a signal drought. surviving low-confidence weeks is table stakes; what separates a resilient Harness config is how fast it course-corrects once quality signal comes back. happy to draft a shared testing playbook if there's appetite.

:raised_hands: yes please to the playbook. if we put it in a Canvas right here it stays evergreen and new folks can self-serve. I'll take a first pass at the structure — metrics, cadence, and a sample test matrix — and drop it in this thread for feedback by end of week.

perfect. let's align on the baseline so the playbook has teeth:
```
Harness QA baseline (v0):
- Signal decay rate: tracked weekly
- False positive revival rate: < 8%
- Prediction drift: flag if > 15% between syncs w/ no new activity
- Time-to-recovery: < 2 syncs after signal returns
```
if your numbers differ wildly from these, shout — that's exactly the kind of gap the calibration pass is meant to catch. great thread all :100:
